item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00367","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C18","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C16 supplies a concrete and material template for the child's overseas coordination provisions. Both assign the Chief of the United States diplomatic mission responsibility for coordinating United States Government activities in each foreign country, ensuring unified execution consistent with foreign policy, and obtaining information from agency representatives. The child broadens this machinery beyond Mutual Security Act programs and embeds it in a larger executive-branch reorganization. C18 and C04 are also closely related sources for the foreign-policy conformity and interagency coordination framework, but C16 has the strongest distinctive textual and functional correspondence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Chief of the United States diplomatic mission in each foreign country must provide effective coordination of, and foreign policy direction with respect to, all United States Government activities in the country.","parent_excerpt":"The Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission in each country... shall coordinate the activities of the United States representatives... in such country... and he shall assume responsibility for assuring the unified development and execution of the said programs in such country.","explanation":"Both place country-level coordination and unified direction under the diplomatic mission chief; the child generalizes C16's Mutual Security program machinery to all United States Government activities."},{"child_excerpt":"The heads of these new agencies should furnish information to the Secretaries of State, Defense, and Treasury... to insure that the program of the agencies and the implementation of such programs conform with foreign policy, military policy, and financial and monetary policy objectives.","parent_excerpt":"All United States representatives affected by this order... shall keep the respective Chiefs of United States Diplomatic Missions and each other fully and currently informed on all matters, including prospective plans, recommendations, and actions... and... shall furnish... documents and information concerning the said programs.","explanation":"The child adapts C16's mandatory information-sharing mechanism to the newly reorganized agencies and relevant Cabinet secretaries."},{"child_excerpt":"The Foreign Operations Administration and the United States Information Agency must seek such guidance and establish appropriate means of assuring that its programs at all times conform to such foreign policy guidance.","parent_excerpt":"Assuring that recommendations and prospective plans and actions of the United States representatives are effectively coordinated and are consistent with and in furtherance of the established policy of the United States.","explanation":"The directives share the operative requirement that agency plans and programs be coordinated and kept consistent with established national foreign policy."}]}
